question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words in the following sentence.
Despite recent superficial moves toward political reconciliation, Libya remains in the grip of a bloodstained corrupt military exclusive circle of people with a common purpose.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. clique.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Clique" means a small, exclusive group of people who share common interests and do not readily allow others to join them. (एक विशिष्ट व्यक्तियों का छोटा समूह)
◦ Example: The new employee found it hard to fit in because of the office clique.

• In the sentence, the phrase "exclusive circle of people with a common purpose" describing Libya's ruling military group is best replaced by the one word "clique", which conveys the same sense of an exclusive, self-serving group.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Oblique (तिरछा/परोक्ष): Slanting in direction, or (of a remark) indirect and not expressed clearly.

• Option 2: Pique (रोष/खिन्नता): A feeling of irritation or resentment, often as the result of a minor offence to one's pride.

• Option 4: Antique (पुरातन वस्तु): An object having value because of its age, especially a piece of furniture or an artwork.

NOTE

• Other words for an exclusive/select group often confused with "clique": coterie (a small exclusive group with shared interests), cabal (a secret political clique), and cartel (a group of businesses combining to restrict competition).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
An instrument for viewing distant objects in space.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Telescope.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Telescope" is an instrument used to view distant objects, especially celestial bodies in space, by making them appear larger and closer. (दूरबीन - दूर की वस्तुओं को देखने का यंत्र)
◦ Example: Astronomers use a powerful telescope to observe distant galaxies.

• The word comes from the Greek "tele" (far) + "skopein" (to look at), literally meaning "far-seer".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Microscope (सूक्ष्मदर्शी): An instrument used to view very small objects that are not visible to the naked eye, not distant objects.

• Option 2: Spectrograph (वर्णक्रम लेखी): An instrument that photographs or records a spectrum of light, used to analyse the composition of light, not simply to view distant objects.

• Option 4: Binoculars (दूरबीन/द्विनेत्री): A hand-held instrument with two eyepieces used for viewing distant objects on Earth; while similar in function, it is not the specific term for an instrument built to view objects in space.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutes with instruments: Microscope (to view minute objects), Periscope (to view objects above the line of sight), Stethoscope (to listen to the heart and lungs), and Kaleidoscope (a tube with mirrors showing changing patterns).

question:
The following sentence contains a word with a spelling error. Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the identified word from the given options.
I was upstaires when somebody rang the doorbell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Upstairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Upstairs" — meaning on or to the upper floor of a building.
◦ Example: She went upstairs to fetch her book.

• Spelling key: UP + STAIRS. The word is a simple compound of "up" and "stairs" (plural), with no extra "e" and no separate "-tares" or "-tires" ending.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Upstares" — incorrect; wrongly replaces "stairs" with "stares", changing the root word entirely.

• Option 2: "Upstaire" — incorrect; the "s" has been dropped from "stairs", making it singular and non-standard.

• Option 3: "upsatires" — incorrect; the letters "a" and "t" have been transposed, and it should also begin with a capital "U" as it starts the sentence.

NOTE

• Commonly confused/misspelt words of this type in SSC exams: downstairs, stairway, staircase. Remember "stairs" always keeps the "s" even in compounds like upstairs/downstairs.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Adversity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Misfortune.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adversity" means a state of difficulty, hardship, or misfortune. (विपत्ति/दुर्भाग्य)
◦ Example: She remained cheerful even in the face of great adversity.

• "Misfortune" also means bad luck or an unfortunate event/condition, making it the closest synonym of "Adversity". (दुर्भाग्य)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Success (सफलता): Achievement of a desired aim or purpose — the opposite of adversity.

• Option 3: Pleasure (आनंद): A feeling of happy satisfaction or enjoyment — unrelated in meaning to hardship.

• Option 4: Advantage (लाभ): A condition or circumstance that puts one in a favourable position — again nearly opposite to adversity.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Adversity": hardship, calamity, distress, affliction, misery.

• Do not confuse "Adversity" (hardship) with "Adversary" (an opponent/enemy) — a common SSC trap.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the following word.
Forbid
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Allow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forbid" means to refuse to allow something; to order someone not to do something. (मना करना)
◦ Example: Smoking is forbidden inside the hospital premises.

• "Allow" means to permit or give permission for something, which is the direct opposite of "Forbid". (अनुमति देना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Prohibit (निषेध करना): To formally forbid something by law or rule — this is a near-synonym of "Forbid", not its opposite.

• Option 3: Call (बुलाना): To summon or name someone/something — unrelated in meaning to "Forbid".

• Option 4: Forsake (त्यागना): To abandon or give up someone/something — again unrelated to permission or prohibition.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Forbid": prohibit, ban, disallow, veto, proscribe.

• Other antonym pairs frequently asked: Permit ↔ Forbid, Sanction ↔ Prohibit, Consent ↔ Refuse.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) while the employees
(B) meeting on time
(C) the boss arrived at the
(D) despite the heavy traffic
(E) were late
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DCBAE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reconstructing the sentence: "Despite the heavy traffic, the boss arrived at the meeting on time while the employees were late."

• Part (D) "despite the heavy traffic" logically opens the sentence as it sets up the contrasting circumstance for what follows.

• Part (C) "the boss arrived at the" must follow, introducing the subject and main verb of the first clause.

• Part (B) "meeting on time" completes the object of "arrived at the", giving "the boss arrived at the meeting on time".

• Parts (A) "while the employees" and (E) "were late" form the contrasting second clause, completing the sentence's meaning of contrast introduced by "despite".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DCBAE.

Additional Information

• Option 2 (DACEB) is incorrect because it produces "despite the heavy traffic while the employees the boss arrived at meeting on time", which is grammatically broken and meaningless.

• Option 3 (BACED) is incorrect because it begins with "meeting on time while the employees...", which has no clear subject-verb opening and does not form a coherent sentence.

• Option 4 (ACEDB) is incorrect because it produces "the employees were late the boss arrived at despite the heavy traffic meeting on time", which is jumbled and does not follow logical clause order.

NOTE

• In parajumbled sentences with "despite/although", the contrasting clause introduced by "despite" often works well as the opening or closing part — always locate the main subject and verb first, then fit the contrasting clause around it.

• Look for connecting words like "while", "and", "but" as clause-joiners to correctly split the sentence into two logical halves.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, ‘On the Origin of Species’, which laid down a treasure of substantiation that evolution occurs, and projected a mechanism, that is, natural selection, for how it does so.
option_1: laid into a treasure of substantiation
option_2: laid about a treasure of substantiation
option_3: laid away a treasure of substantiation
option_4: laid out a treasure of substantiation
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. laid out a treasure of substantiation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "lay out" means to present, explain, or set forth something systematically and in detail. (विस्तार से प्रस्तुत करना/स्पष्ट करना)
◦ Example: The report lays out the company's plans for the next five years.

• In the sentence, Darwin's book is said to have thoroughly presented a wealth of evidence ("a treasure of substantiation") that evolution occurs — this sense of detailed presentation is best expressed by "laid out".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "laid into" means to attack or criticise someone/something forcefully — it does not fit the context of presenting evidence.

• Option 2: "laid about" means to hit out wildly in all directions (physically attack) — again unrelated to presenting evidence.

• Option 3: "laid away" is not a standard idiomatic phrasal verb in this context; "lay away" usually refers to reserving goods by making part payment, which does not fit here.

NOTE

• Other useful "lay" phrasal verbs for SSC: lay off (to dismiss employees), lay down (to formulate a rule, or to sacrifice), lay up (to store for future use, or to be confined by illness), lay aside (to save or set apart).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
It is he who work for the company for more than a decade.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. who work.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "It is he who work for the company for more than a decade" contains a subject-verb agreement error.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement with relative pronouns: When "who" refers back to a singular subject (here, "he"), the verb that follows "who" must also be in the singular form.

• Here, "who" refers to "he" (third person singular), so the verb must be "works", not "work".
◦ Correct: It is he who works for the company for more than a decade.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "for more than a decade" is grammatically correct — it correctly expresses a duration using "for".

• Option 3: "for the company" is grammatically correct — a proper prepositional phrase indicating the object of employment.

• Option 4: "It is he" is grammatically correct — the correct subjective case "he" is used, not the objective "him", as it functions as the subject complement.

NOTE

• With relative pronouns (who/which/that), always check the noun/pronoun they refer back to, and match the verb to that antecedent, not to any noun that appears closer to the verb.

• Similar structures to watch for: "It is I who am...", "It is they who are...", "It is she who has..."

question:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
The teachers of our school have already taken this training.
option_1: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.
option_2: This training has been taken by the teachers of our school.
option_3: This training has already been taken by the our school teachers.
option_4: This training was already taken by the teachers of our school.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The teachers of our school have already taken this training" is in the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "this training" becomes the subject; since it is singular/uncountable, the auxiliary is "has"; the adverb "already" is placed between the auxiliary and "been"; the verb "taken" (already V3) is retained; and "the teachers of our school" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because it drops the word "already", changing the meaning/emphasis of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "the our school teachers" is an ungrammatical phrase — a possessive/article cannot be used this way; it should remain "the teachers of our school".

• Option 4 is incorrect because "was already taken" is Simple Past Tense passive, not Present Perfect Tense passive.

NOTE

• Words like "already", "just", "never", "ever" are placed immediately after the first auxiliary verb (has/have) in both active and passive Present Perfect sentences.

• Common SSC trap: changing the tense of the auxiliary verb (has/have → was/were) while converting voice, which alters the tense of the sentence and is always incorrect unless the original sentence demands it.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
He was very cruel in dealing with the students.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Kind.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cruel" means causing pain or suffering to others deliberately; showing no mercy. (क्रूर)
◦ Example: It was cruel of him to leave the injured dog on the road.

• "Kind" means having or showing a friendly, generous, and considerate nature, which is the direct opposite of "Cruel". (दयालु)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Skittish (चंचल/डरपोक): Nervous, easily frightened, or restless (often used for animals) — unrelated to cruelty.

• Option 3: Malevolent (द्वेषपूर्ण): Having or showing a wish to do evil to others — this is actually a synonym, not an antonym, of "Cruel".

• Option 4: Kingly (राजसी): Belonging to or resembling a king; majestic — unrelated in meaning to "Cruel" or "Kind".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Cruel": brutal, ruthless, merciless, savage, callous.

• Other antonym pairs: Merciless ↔ Compassionate, Ruthless ↔ Gentle, Savage ↔ Civil/Humane.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
(A) he had to take the bus
(B) his friend, who used to give
(C) to his office because he had
(D) him a lift, was on vacation
(E) never learned to drive and
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ACEBD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reconstructing the sentence: "He had to take the bus to his office because he had never learned to drive and his friend, who used to give him a lift, was on vacation."

• Part (A) "he had to take the bus" opens the sentence, introducing the main subject and action.

• Part (C) "to his office because he had" follows to state the destination and begin the reason clause.

• Part (E) "never learned to drive and" completes the first reason (inability to drive) and connects to the second reason with "and".

• Parts (B) "his friend, who used to give" and (D) "him a lift, was on vacation" together form the second reason, explaining that his usual means of transport (his friend) was unavailable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ACEBD.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DACEB) is incorrect because it begins with "him a lift, was on vacation", which has no clear subject and does not open the sentence logically.

• Option 3 (EBADC) is incorrect because it begins with "never learned to drive and", which cannot stand as the opening of the sentence without an established subject.

• Option 4 (BADEC) is incorrect because it produces "his friend, who used to give he had to take the bus...", which is grammatically broken and incoherent.

NOTE

• In parajumbled sentences containing a relative clause (introduced by "who"), first locate the noun the clause describes (here, "his friend") and keep the clause attached immediately after it.

• Reason clauses introduced by "because" typically follow the main clause they explain — locate the main action first, then attach the reason.

question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
Ravi will play the match.
option_1: The match is played by Ravi.
option_2: The match will have been played by Ravi.
option_3: The match will be playing by Ravi.
option_4: The match will be played by Ravi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The match will be played by Ravi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Ravi will play the match" is in the Simple Future Tense.

• Rule — Simple Future Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the match" becomes the subject; the modal "will" is retained, followed by "be"; the verb "play" becomes the past participle "played"; and "Ravi" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: The match will be played by Ravi.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is played" is Simple Present Tense passive, not Simple Future Tense passive.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "will have been played" is the passive form of the Future Perfect Tense, not the Simple Future Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "will be playing" wrongly uses the continuous form after "be"; the correct passive auxiliary structure after "will" is "be + V3" (played), not "be + playing".

NOTE

• The passive voice cannot normally be formed for the Future Continuous and Future Perfect Continuous tenses in standard usage — remember: only Simple Future and Future Perfect have regular passive forms: "will be + V3" and "will have been + V3" respectively.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
Our legal system must frame proper legal rules for juvenile criminals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. young.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Juvenile" means relating to or characteristic of young people; not fully grown. (किशोर/नाबालिग)
◦ Example: The court has a separate system for dealing with juvenile offenders.

• "Young" means not yet old; in an early stage of life, which best conveys the same sense as "juvenile" in the given sentence about criminals who are minors. (युवा/कम उम्र का)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Senile (जराजीर्ण): Showing a loss of mental faculties due to old age — nearly opposite in meaning to "juvenile".

• Option 2: Dotage (बुढ़ापा/जराजीर्णता): The period of life when a person is old and weak, especially with declining mental faculties — again related to old age, opposite of "juvenile".

• Option 3: Old (बूढ़ा): Having lived for a long time; aged — opposite in meaning to "juvenile".

NOTE

• Related legal terms often tested: "Juvenile Justice" (the legal system dealing with offences by minors), "Juvenile delinquency" (criminal behaviour by young people).

• Do not confuse "Juvenile" (young) with "Senile"/"Dotage" (old age related) — a common SSC antonym trap in the same options set.

question:
Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom.
The doctors tried very hard to save his mother but they were unsuccessful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. moved heaven and earth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to move heaven and earth" means to make every possible effort; to try extremely hard to achieve something. (कुछ पाने के लिए भरसक प्रयास करना)
◦ Example: They moved heaven and earth to find a cure for their son's illness.

• In the sentence, the doctors made every possible effort to save the patient's mother, which is exactly the sense conveyed by this idiom.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To face the music (परिणाम भुगतना): To accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions.

• Option 2: To draw the line (सीमा तय करना): To set a limit on what one is willing to do or accept.

• Option 4: To run like clockwork (सुचारू रूप से चलना): To proceed smoothly and without any problems, exactly as planned.

NOTE

• Other idioms meaning "to try very hard": "leave no stone unturned", "go all out", "put one's best foot forward", "burn the midnight oil" (to work hard, especially late at night).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Hit the nail on the head
option_2: They have accurately identified or explained something.
option_4: They hit a nail with a hammer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. They have accurately identified or explained something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to hit the nail on the head" means to describe or identify exactly what is causing a situation or problem; to be precisely correct about something. (बिल्कुल सही बात कहना/सटीक अनुमान लगाना)
◦ Example: When she said the problem was poor communication, she hit the nail on the head.

• The idiom draws on the image of striking a nail's head precisely and squarely with a hammer — i.e., getting something exactly right.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "They are experiencing a headache" is a literal misreading of "nail on the head" and is not the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 3: "They're uncertain about a decision" is incorrect; the idiom conveys certainty and accuracy, not uncertainty.

• Option 4: "They hit a nail with a hammer" is the literal, non-idiomatic meaning of the words and is not what the idiom conveys.

NOTE

• Other idioms of accuracy/correctness often asked in SSC: "spot on" (exactly correct), "on the money" (accurate), "strike the right chord" (to say or do something that produces a positive response).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
The windows / violent banged / during the / storm yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. violent banged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The windows violent banged during the storm yesterday" contains an error of word form — an adjective has been wrongly used in place of an adverb.

• Rule — Adjective vs Adverb: A verb (here, "banged") must be modified by an adverb, not an adjective. Adjectives modify nouns/pronouns, while adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.

• "Violent" is an adjective and cannot modify the verb "banged"; it must be changed to the adverb "violently".
◦ Correct: The windows banged violently during the storm yesterday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "during the" is grammatically correct — a standard preposition + article combination.

• Option 2: "The windows" is grammatically correct — a proper noun phrase acting as the subject.

• Option 3: "storm yesterday." is grammatically correct — "yesterday" correctly functions as a time adverb modifying the action in this part of the sentence.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner are usually formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective (violent → violently, quick → quickly), and they answer the question "how?" about the action of the verb.

• Common SSC trap: using the adjective form immediately before or after a verb where an adverb is grammatically required, e.g., "She sang beautiful" (incorrect) vs. "She sang beautifully" (correct).

question:
Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options.
His acquiantance with the author led to many fruitful collaborations.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. acquaintance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Acquaintance" — a person one knows slightly, or the state of knowing someone slightly.
◦ Example: He is not a close friend, just an acquaintance from college.

• Spelling key: AC + QUAINT + ANCE. Remember the base word "quaint" is embedded inside, and the ending is "-ance", not "-ence" or "-ense".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "acuiantance" — incorrect; the letter "q" has been dropped and "u" wrongly follows "c" directly.

• Option 3: "acquaintence" — incorrect; the ending should be "-ance", not "-ence".

• Option 4: "aquaintance" — incorrect; the letter "c" has been dropped after the initial "a".

NOTE

• Related word forms: acquaint (verb), acquainted (adjective).

• Other commonly misspelt "-ance/-ence" ending words in SSC: maintenance, appearance, occurrence, existence, correspondence.

question:
Identify the correct synonym of the word given below.
FATIGUE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Tiredness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fatigue" means extreme tiredness resulting from physical or mental exertion. (थकान)
◦ Example: After the long trek, the climbers were overcome with fatigue.

• "Tiredness" also means the state of feeling in need of rest or sleep; weariness, making it the closest synonym of "Fatigue". (थकान)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Mission (अभियान/लक्ष्य): An important assignment or task given to a person or group — unrelated in meaning to tiredness.

• Option 3: Vigour (जोश/शक्ति): Physical strength and good health; energy and enthusiasm — nearly opposite to "Fatigue".

• Option 4: Obese (मोटा/स्थूल): Grossly overweight — unrelated in meaning to "Fatigue".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Fatigue": exhaustion, weariness, lethargy, lassitude.

• Do not confuse "Fatigue" (tiredness) with the unrelated military term "fatigues" (soldier's work uniform), which sometimes appears as a distractor in reading passages.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
She was overstrung before her dance performance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nervous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Overstrung" means extremely nervous, tense, or easily excited/agitated. (अत्यधिक उत्तेजित/घबराया हुआ)
◦ Example: She felt overstrung and could not sit still before the interview.

• "Nervous" means easily agitated or anxious; apprehensive, which conveys the same emotional state as "overstrung" in the given sentence about a dance performance. (घबराया हुआ)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Cheerful (प्रसन्न): Noticeably happy and optimistic — opposite in meaning to "overstrung".

• Option 2: Calm (शांत): Not showing or feeling nervousness or anger — opposite in meaning to "overstrung".

• Option 3: Placid (शांत/स्थिर): Not easily upset or excited — again, nearly opposite to "overstrung".

NOTE

• "Overstrung" originally describes a piano with overlapping (crossed) strings, and figuratively came to mean a person whose "strings" (nerves) are stretched too tight, i.e. highly strung/tense.

• Other synonyms for a nervous emotional state: agitated, jittery, edgy, on edge, highly strung.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Awkward in movement or manner
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Clumsy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Clumsy" means awkward in movement or in handling things; lacking grace or skill. (अनाड़ी/भद्दा)
◦ Example: He knocked over the vase because he was so clumsy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Alert (सतर्क): Quick to notice and respond to things; watchful — unrelated to awkwardness of movement.

• Option 2: Imbalanced (असंतुलित): Lacking balance or proportion; not evenly distributed — describes a state, not the manner of movement itself, and is not the standard one-word substitute for this definition.

• Option 4: Clownish (विदूषक जैसा): Behaving like a clown; comically silly or foolish — related to comic behaviour, not simply awkward movement.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutes describing manner/behaviour often asked in SSC: Gauche (socially awkward or tactless), Ungainly (awkward, clumsy in movement), Graceful (the antonym — moving in an elegant, controlled way).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an (1) _________ by the Government of India to celebrate and remember 75 years of independence and the beautiful history of its people, culture and achievements. This Mahotsav is (2) _________ to the people of India, who have not only been instrumental in bringing India this far in its evolutionary journey but also (3) _________ the power and potential to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's (4) _________ of activating India 2.0, fuelled by the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The formal journey of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav began on 12 March 2021, beginning a (5)______ to our 75th anniversary of independence and will finish a year later on 15 August 2023.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 1.%
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. initiative.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun describing a planned action or programme undertaken by the Government of India, followed by "by the Government of India to celebrate...".

• "Initiative" means a new plan or programme for doing something; an act of starting a process, which correctly describes "Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav" as a government programme.
◦ Correct: Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an initiative by the Government of India...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "associate" means a partner or colleague, or (as a verb) to connect; it does not fit as a noun describing a government programme.

• Option 3: "obligation" means a duty or legal/moral requirement to do something — this does not fit the sense of a celebratory programme.

• Option 4: "occult" means relating to supernatural or magical powers/practices — completely unrelated to the context.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always check whether the blank needs a noun, verb, adjective, or adverb by examining the surrounding article ("an") and preposition ("by") — here "an ___ by the Government" clearly demands a singular noun.

• Words related to government programmes often tested: scheme, initiative, campaign, mission, movement.

Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an (1) _________ by the Government of India to celebrate and remember 75 years of independence and the beautiful history of its people, culture and achievements. This Mahotsav is (2) _________ to the people of India, who have not only been instrumental in bringing India this far in its evolutionary journey but also (3) _________ the power and potential to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's (4) _________ of activating India 2.0, fuelled by the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The formal journey of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav began on 12 March 2021, beginning a (5)______ to our 75th anniversary of independence and will finish a year later on 15 August 2023.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 2.%
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. dedicated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word describing the Mahotsav's relationship to "the people of India" — that it is devoted or offered to them in recognition of their role.

• "Dedicated" means devoted to a particular purpose or, as used here, offered/devoted to a person or group in tribute, which fits the sense that the Mahotsav is devoted to honouring the people of India.
◦ Correct: This Mahotsav is dedicated to the people of India, who have not only been instrumental...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "alienated" means estranged or made to feel isolated — this contradicts the positive, celebratory tone of the passage.

• Option 3: "refused" means declined or rejected — it does not make sense to say the Mahotsav is "refused to the people of India".

• Option 4: "withhold" means to hold back or refuse to give — again contrary to the celebratory, honouring tone of the passage, and also the wrong verb form after "is".

NOTE

• "Dedicated to" is a common fixed collocation meaning devoted or given in honour of someone/something — frequently tested in SSC cloze passages.

• Contrast with near-opposite words like "alienated from" and "withheld from", which signal negative or distancing relationships — always check whether the passage's tone is positive or negative before choosing.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an (1) _________ by the Government of India to celebrate and remember 75 years of independence and the beautiful history of its people, culture and achievements. This Mahotsav is (2) _________ to the people of India, who have not only been instrumental in bringing India this far in its evolutionary journey but also (3) _________ the power and potential to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's (4) _________ of activating India 2.0, fuelled by the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The formal journey of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav began on 12 March 2021, beginning a (5)______ to our 75th anniversary of independence and will finish a year later on 15 August 2023.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 3.%
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. possess.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank continues the relative clause "who have not only been instrumental... but also ___ the power and potential", requiring a verb parallel to "have been" and agreeing with the plural subject "people of India".

• "Possess" means to have or own something (here, a quality/capability), which correctly fits "possess the power and potential to realise..." in agreement with the plural subject.
◦ Correct: ...but also possess the power and potential to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's vision...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "clarifies" means to make something clearer or easier to understand; besides being contextually wrong, it is singular and does not agree with the plural subject "people".

• Option 3: "concludes" means to bring to an end or to deduce; it does not fit the sense of "having" power and potential, and is also singular in form.

• Option 4: "obtains" means to get or acquire something; besides not agreeing with the plural subject, it wrongly suggests acquiring rather than already possessing the power and potential.

NOTE

• With the correlative structure "not only... but also", the verb after "but also" must remain grammatically parallel in tense and number to the verb used after "not only" ("have been") — here, both must agree with the plural subject "people".

• Watch subject-verb agreement carefully in cloze passages — a contextually appealing word can still be the wrong option if it does not agree in number with its subject.

Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an (1) _________ by the Government of India to celebrate and remember 75 years of independence and the beautiful history of its people, culture and achievements. This Mahotsav is (2) _________ to the people of India, who have not only been instrumental in bringing India this far in its evolutionary journey but also (3) _________ the power and potential to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's (4) _________ of activating India 2.0, fuelled by the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The formal journey of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav began on 12 March 2021, beginning a (5)______ to our 75th anniversary of independence and will finish a year later on 15 August 2023.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 4.%
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. vision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun following the possessive "Narendra Modi's ___ of activating India 2.0", describing an aspirational plan or foresight for the country's future.

• "Vision" means the ability to think about or plan the future with imagination or wisdom; a mental image of what the future could or should be, which correctly fits "Modi's vision of activating India 2.0".
◦ Correct: ...to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's vision of activating India 2.0...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "graphics" refers to visual images or designs, typically produced by computer — unrelated to a leader's plan for national development.

• Option 3: "design" means a plan or drawing for the construction of something, or a general plan/scheme; while plausible, it does not carry the aspirational, forward-looking sense that "vision" does, and is less contextually precise here since the passage speaks of "realising" a future goal.

• Option 4: "control" means the power to influence or direct behaviour; it does not fit the sense of an aspirational plan being "realised".

NOTE

• "Vision" is commonly used in the context of leadership and national development to mean a guiding long-term goal, e.g., "Vision 2020", "visionary leader".

• Words often confused in such contexts: vision (foresight/aspiration), mission (the actionable purpose), goal (the specific target), objective (a measurable aim).

The formal journey of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav began on 12 March 2021, beginning a (5)______ to our 75th anniversary of independence and will finish a year later on 15 August 2023.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank number 5.%
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. countdown.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun following "beginning a ___ to our 75th anniversary of independence", describing the period leading up to a significant milestone date.

• "Countdown" means the act of counting backwards to zero as a way of measuring the time remaining before an event, which correctly fits the sense of a journey building up towards the 75th anniversary.
◦ Correct: ...beginning a countdown to our 75th anniversary of independence and will finish a year later on 15 August 2023.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "allocation" means the action of distributing resources for a particular purpose — unrelated to counting down towards a date.

• Option 3: "custom" means a traditional way of behaving or a practice — it does not fit the sense of a time-bound journey towards an anniversary.

• Option 4: "breakdown" means a failure or collapse (mechanical, or of negotiations/health), or a division of something into parts — neither sense fits the context of building up towards a celebration.

NOTE

• "Countdown to" is a common fixed collocation used for events approaching a specific date, e.g., "the countdown to the Olympics has begun".

• In cloze passages, always match the chosen word not just to the immediate blank but to the overall theme and tone of the passage — here, a celebratory build-up to an anniversary.
